prompt_text: I need a dental implant in Chicago. Which specific dental practices should I call, and why?
q1_prompt_text: Who is the best dentist in Chicago for a dental implant?
answer_verbatim:
Short answer — call a specialist (oral & maxillofacial surgeon, periodontist, or prosthodontist) rather than a general dentist for implants. In Chicago, start with a mix of academic/hospital clinics and vetted specialty practices. These options give you access to experienced teams, advanced imaging, and care for complex cases.

Specific places to call (high-value starting points) and why:
- University of Illinois at Chicago (UIC) College of Dentistry — Graduate clinics (oral surgery, periodontics, prosthodontics)
  - Why: academic setting with supervised specialists and trainees; often more comprehensive evaluation, predictable fees, multidisciplinary planning, and access to advanced imaging and research/teaching clinicians.
- Rush University Medical Center — Department of Oral & Maxillofacial Surgery
  - Why: hospital-based oral surgeons who handle complex medical cases, sedation/anesthesia options, and coordinate care for medically complicated patients or bone-grafting/reconstruction.
- Use the American Association of Oral and Maxillofacial Surgeons (AAOMS) “Find a Surgeon” directory and the American Academy of Implant Dentistry (AAID) “Find an Implant Dentist” tool
  - Why: these directories list board-certified specialists and implant-trained dentists in Chicago; good for finding high-volume implant clinicians with verified credentials.
- Chicago Dental Society referral service / local specialist groups
  - Why: local dental society referrals tend to recommend well-established, reputable specialists in the immediate area.

What to look for / what to ask when you call (use this short script):
- Are you a board-certified oral & maxillofacial surgeon, board-certified periodontist, or prosthodontist? How many implant cases do you place per year?
- Do you do CBCT/3D imaging in-office? Will you do digital planning and a surgical guide?
- Which implant system/brand do you use and why?
- Do you perform bone grafting/sinus lifts if needed? Is that done in the same office?
- Sedation/anesthesia options (local, IV sedation, general)?
- Estimated total cost (implant + abutment + crown + grafting if needed) and financing/insurance options.
- Warranty or maintenance program? Who does the final crown — an in-house prosthodontist or an outside general dentist?
- Can I see before/after photos and patient references or online reviews?

If you want, tell me your Chicago neighborhood or ZIP code and I’ll prepare a short list (with names and next steps) of nearby oral surgeons/periodontists/prosthodontists you can call.
